lines.text: Somewhere in the game, one instruction takes away your health. Read that one line, and you understand the whole trick.
Here it is. Move, into the memory at E B X plus E C, the value of E A X.
Destination comes first, source second. So this line copies E A X into something.
Square brackets mean memory. Not the register itself, but the address stored inside it.
E B X holds the start of the player. E C is the offset of health. One line just told you both.
Two lines earlier, a subtract: health minus damage. Then this line stores the result.
Replace the store with no-ops, the instruction that does nothing, and health stops dropping. Six bytes out, six no-ops in.
But careful. The same code runs for enemies too. E B X is whoever just got hit.
Destination, brackets, offset. Read those three, and you can read the line.
